what: the day's ranked clusters, in the desk's own one line, sources counted and linked (Jack, 5 October 2026)
what_a_wire_line_is: Each line is the desk's own one-line summary of a story it ranked, with its sources counted and linked. It is not a story the desk wrote or checked; only the item with a badge was checked.

items.line: Brooklyn DA and FBI dismantled Russian-language crypto scam network, seizing 112 servers and shutting 241 domains after victims lost tens of millions.
titles: How Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI took down a massive crypto fraud network targeting Russian speakers
FBI helps smash crypto scam targeting Russian speakers in Brooklyn

items.line: EU banking authority classified Circle's USDC as 'significant' e-money token under MiCA, activating Nov. 12 supervisory rules.
titles: EBA designates Circle’s USDC as the EU’s first ‘significant’ e-money token

items.line: Solana confirmed Oct. 21 Alpenglow upgrade, replacing TowerBFT voting to cut finality from 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds.
titles: Solana Sets a Date for Its Next Major Upgrade

items.line: Australia's ASIC proposed stricter rules for crypto exchange licensing, including capital and custody requirements due ahead of 2027 rollout.
titles: Australia’s financial watchdog seeks stiffer rules for crypto exchanges ahead of licensing deadline

items.line: Russia's Central Bank confirmed ban on direct P2P crypto trades effective July 1, 2027, requiring residents to use authorized intermediaries.
titles: Russia Will Soon Ban Peer-to-Peer Bitcoin Trading, Central Bank Confirms

items.line: Hot US producer-price data triggered nearly $940 million in crypto liquidations as Fed rate-hike bets spiked to 50%.
titles: Nearly $1 billion in crypto bets liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slide

checked.says: CoinDesk reports the scheme stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, with a recovery scam targeting victims again; authorities seized 241 domains and 112 servers.
checked.unconfirmed: The exact dollar total of losses is described as 'tens of millions' but not quantified precisely; Protos reports $300,000 seized by Gonzalez's office but the full victim loss amount is not stated.
